# Server flags

`python -m decisio.serve.vllm_engine`, decisio 0.33.0 <!-- x-release-please-version -->.
A dash in the default column means the flag has no default of its own: it takes the base's value, or is off.
`docs/cli.md` says which value each base takes.

| Flag | Default | Values | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--base` | - | text | the base model and its served settings (decisio.families; README, 'Choosing a base'): gemma-4-31b (the default; served from its FP8 repository, tachara-ai/decisio-gemma-4-31b), qwen3.6-35b-a3b (Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8), gemma-4-12b (google/gemma-4-12B-it, bf16) or gemma-4-12b-fp8 (the same checkpoint quantized to FP8 on load, the 12B's second precision) or gemma-4-31b-bf16 (google/gemma-4-31B-it as published, not quantized, the 31B's second precision; it needs a card with room for 58 GiB of weights and a KV cache), each at a pinned revision; or a decisio repository, owner/name[@revision] or a directory holding decision_config.json (docs/running.md). Every setting below that says 'the base's' takes the base's value unless given. Without --base, the base is detected from --model's config.json |
| `--model` | - | text | the checkpoint: a local directory or a Hugging Face repository id (default: the base's own checkpoint; for gemma-4-31b that is tachara-ai/decisio-gemma-4-31b, and --model google/gemma-4-31B-it serves Google's weights instead, quantized to FP8 on load) |
| `--revision` | - | text | the checkpoint's revision on the Hugging Face hub (default: the base's pinned revision when --model is the base's own checkpoint) |
| `--mode` | `separate` | `separate`, `packed` |  |
| `--pad-to` | - | text | 'block', a token count, or 'none' (separate mode); default: the base's (Qwen: block; Gemma: none) |
| `--pad-where` | `front` | `between`, `front`, `user` |  |
| `--adapter` | - | text, repeatable | name=path of a vLLM-format LoRA adapter |
| `--default-adapter` | - | `NAME` | answer a request that names no adapter with this loaded adapter (one of the --adapter names), with its own temperatures, as when it is named. A request that names another loaded adapter gets that one, and "adapter": "none" gets the base. Shown in /health and the serving-stack fingerprint; registering and certifying tasks still read the base |
| `--adapter-temperatures` | - | text, repeatable | name=file of a decisio.adapter/1 file of that adapter's temperatures per question type (choice, noul, score) and, for choice, optionally per band of option count (choice_bands), served for a request that names it; replaces the decisio_adapter.json in its folder; repeatable |
| `--pack` | `16` | `int` |  |
| `--pad-policy` | - | `always`, `shared`, `row`, `none` | always (the default with vLLM): front-pad every state to the block; shared: pad only when the request has more than one question to share the padded boundary (a single-question request then reads its state unpadded, a different prompt); row: a single-question request is front-padded so its whole row, state and question, ends on the block boundary and is prefilled in one engine step (multi-question requests as always); none (the default with --backend mlx, whose cache needs no padding): never pad, so a question asked alone and inside a request is one prompt (resolve_pad_policy) |
| `--multi-question` | - | `sequential`, `warm`, `batch` | sequential (the served default; gemma-4-31b's is warm with the engine in the server's process): a request with several questions first prefills the state in a warm-up request, then sends each question in its own engine call, reading the state from the prefix cache, so every answer equals the question sent alone; warm (for bulk scoring): the warm-up, then every question in one batch, faster but each answer depends on the batch; batch: one engine call with every question, each prefilling the state itself, no warm-up |
| `--concurrency` | `serial` | `serial`, `batched` | serial (the default): one request at a time through the engine, so a request's answer is a function of the request alone, whatever else the server is sent; batched: the requests waiting for the engine are scored together in one engine call (up to --batch-max-requests), more throughput under concurrent load (measured on the FP8 12B, new 1,000-token states, 8 and 16 clients; measure on your own traffic), but an answer can differ slightly with the traffic it arrived with (docs/running.md, 'Concurrency'). A lone request is scored as a serial server scores it. The mode is in /health and in the serving-stack fingerprint: a certificate made under one mode is not served as certified under the other |
| `--batch-max-requests` | `16` | `int` | --concurrency batched: the most requests in one engine call (default 16); it counts requests, not rows, and the oldest waiting request is always taken, however many questions it has |
| `--register-boundary` | - | `after`, `before`, `off` | on a base that registers a state's boundary for the next question (the Gemma bases; /health registers_state_boundary), where a single question on a new state registers it: after, once the response is out, so the caller does not wait for it and a question sent after the answer reads the state from the cache; before (the default of both Gemma bases), ahead of the question; off, never, so a later question about the state reads it again (docs/running.md) |
| `--engine-process` | - | `in`, `separate` | where vLLM's engine runs: in (the server's process, VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0), where a request's questions always share one engine step, so --multi-question warm repeats exactly; separate (vLLM's own arrangement, a process of its own). The default resolves to in for a single-engine server and to separate with a second engine (--image-model, --head-engine, --one-engine), with which in is refused |
| `--engine` | `{"compilation_config": {"max_cudagraph_capture_size": 4096}}` | text | extra LLM(...) keyword arguments as JSON |
| `--model-class` | - | `hidden-readout`, `text-only`, `view` | hidden-readout (the default): --model is the official checkpoint, loaded under decisio's registered text-only class that also returns the hidden state at the answer position, so registered tasks fit and serve an intent head from this one engine; text-only (the default with --head-engine): the same class without the hidden state; view: --model is a directory vLLM loads as it is, the text-only view built by decisio.serve.make_text_only (the fallback that needs no plugin). The decisio classes need the package installed, so vLLM's engine processes find the plugin through its entry point |
| `--allow-deep-gemm` | off | on or off | start even when VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM is set to something other than 0 (default: refuse) |
| `--backend` | `vllm` | `vllm`, `hf`, `mlx` | hf: the CPU stand-in (decisio.serve.hf_letters), for the CPU smoke test only; mlx: Apple silicon (decisio.serve.mlx_engine), --model an MLX conversion, the text route with every feature except the image route, packed mode and adapters |
| `--prefix-cache-mb` | - | `int` | --backend mlx: the budget of the cross-request prefix cache in MiB (the base's: 2048 for the Qwen base, 7400 for gemma-4-12b; 0 turns it off): a request whose state prefix was seen before continues from its kept cache instead of prefilling it, with the same answers bit for bit |
| `--mlx-memory-limit-gb` | - | `float` | --backend mlx: MLX's memory limit in GiB. Default: what the base needs (its weights, its working set at a 32k-token state, the cache limit, the prefix cache and 2 GiB of headroom), never above two thirds of the machine's memory; 0 leaves MLX's own, about 80 percent of the memory, which a server that answers many states grows into. The server refuses to start when the base does not fit (docs/running.md, 'Memory on a Mac') |
| `--mlx-cache-limit-gb` | - | `float` | --backend mlx: MLX's cache limit in GiB, the freed buffers it keeps for reuse (default 2) |
| `--tokenizer` | - | text | --backend mlx: the tokenizer the prompts are built with, a directory, a repository or repo@revision (default: the base's official one, its checkpoint at its revision in decisio.families, so the prompts are the vLLM path's byte for byte; a conversion's own tokenizer may differ) |
| `--served-name` | - | text | the name GET /v1/models lists (default: the base's; Qwen: decisio-qwen3.6-35b-a3b-letters) |
| `--orders` | `1` | `1`, `2` | /v1/systemone: 2 = two-order averaging (after Reflex); the per-question disagreement goes to --branch-log |
| `--branch-log` | - | text | JSONL of two-order branches and their disagreement |
| `--image-model` | - | text | the full multimodal checkpoint: a second engine under the multimodal class, serving only /v1/systemone requests that carry images (decisio.serve.image_engine); the text route is unchanged |
| `--max-images` | - | `int` | the most images one request may carry on the --image-model engine (default 128: 128 images of 512 by 512 pixels fill the context, so for photos the context ends a request; lower it to save the multimodal profiling memory at start-up, raise it for smaller images) |
| `--hide-index-keys` / `--no-hide-index-keys` | on | on or off | /v1/systemone: show only the descriptions of options whose keys are a pure enumeration (option_0, option_1, ...), never the index beside our letters (default on; --no-hide-index-keys renders `key: description` as before) |
| `--desnake-labels` / `--no-desnake-labels` | on | on or off | /v1/systemone: when options are shown as bare labels and every label is snake_case (card_arrival, ...), show them with spaces (default on; --no-desnake-labels leaves them) |
| `--describe-options` / `--no-describe-options` | on | on or off | /v1/systemone: show an option that has a description as its description alone, with no key; an option without one as its key (default on; --no-describe-options shows `key: description`; the keys stay the answer's keys) |
| `--noul-rendering` | - | `words`, `letters`, `letters-keys` | /v1/systemone: how a yes/no question is asked (default: the base's; Qwen letters-keys, Gemma letters). letters-keys: a two-option choice, the false side first, the sides named ('No: ...', 'Yes: ...'), read from the letters; letters: as letters-keys with each side shown as its criteria description alone ('No' and 'Yes' without one); words: the instructions with 'Yes means' and 'No means' lines, read from the yes and no tokens. Abstention and two-order requests keep words |
| `--abstention` / `--no-abstention` | on | on or off | /v1/systemone: apply registered per-task abstention thresholds (POST /v1/abstention/tasks; decisio.serve.abstention); --no-abstention ignores them (default on; no task, no change) |
| `--abstention-tasks` | - | text | a JSON list of tasks to load at start (as the endpoint returns them) |
| `--abstain-option` | - | text | offer this extra option (e.g. "can't tell") on every question of requests that use imajev's extension, and report its probability as unknown_probability / abstained; untrained, opt-in |
| `--system-prompt` / `--no-system-prompt` | - | on or off | a system turn before each question (decisio.readout.system_prompt); default: the base's (Gemma: on, Qwen: off) |
| `--prompt-tail` | - | `compact`, `spaced` | the question's layout and last line (default: the base's, spaced for both): spaced (a blank line before and after the lettered options, then one line asking for the chosen option's letter alone, decisio.readout.spaced), or compact (for tasks fitted under it; no blank lines, 'Answer with the letter only.'). Tasks registered under one are not applied under the other |
| `--flavor` | - | `calibrated`, `commit`, `read-enhanced` | serve a named configuration of the base (docs/design/flavors.md): calibrated (calibrated probabilities for every type), commit (commits yes/no answers outside the uncertain middle band) or read-enhanced (reads short requests twice). Every flavor uses the header layout; the server is named Decisio-31b-<flavor>, Decisio-12b-<flavor> or Decisio-12b-fp8-<flavor>. A flag you give still wins and is recorded as an override (/health, x-decisio-flavor, the start line, the fingerprint). Gemma bases only; not with a tuned repository. Without it the server is what it was |
| `--layout` | - | `plain`, `header` | the user turn's layout. header (the default of the Gemma bases) lists the request's questions before the state ('Questions that will be asked about the context:' and a '- <question>' line each), then the state and the question as plain; plain is the state then the question (the Qwen base's default, and what the Gemma bases were served with before the header became theirs). Without the flag the server holds plain while it loads tasks fitted under plain, or an adapter or tuned repository that recorded no layout (the start says so). A state cached for one set of questions is not reused for another under header: a client that asks a series of questions about one state wants plain. Tasks fitted and certificates made under one layout are not applied under another (docs/running.md) |
| `--read-twice-under` | - | `N` | read short requests twice (off; never the default): when a request read once is at most N counted input tokens (the header, the state and each question's text: what usage.input_tokens reports for it), each question's user turn is written twice, joined by 'Read the same input again before answering:'. It roughly doubles the input tokens of the requests it applies to, and usage.input_tokens counts both copies. Measured on the 31B with the header: N = 2000 was the smallest within 0.25 points of the best on our proxies (+3.2) and gave +1.8 on a public multi-domain sample with p80 about 866 ms; a threshold of 3000 counted on rows is at or over a 1,000 ms p80 target. Pair it with --read-twice-max-questions. Tasks and certificates are per setting (docs/running.md) |
| `--read-twice-max-questions` | - | `R` | with --read-twice-under: a request with more than R questions is read once, whatever its size (default: no cap). A doubled request costs more with every question, which the token count does not see, so R is what keeps a latency target: set it from a timing run on your card (the largest question count whose doubled request at N = 2000 stays under about 900 ms) |
| `--answer-slot` | - | `prefill`, `template` | where the label is read: after 'Answer:' prefilled in the assistant turn (prefill; the Qwen base's), or at the chat template's own first assistant position (template; the Gemma base's) |
| `--label-variants` | - | `single`, `summed` | the tokens read per label: single (the Qwen base's; one, the form the slot reads), or summed (the Gemma base's; every single-token form: ' A', 'A' and a byte-fallback token where there is one; ' yes', 'yes', ' Yes' and 'Yes'; their probabilities summed) |
| `--temperature` | - | `float` | /v1/systemone: the global temperature on the text route's plain readout, softmax(log p / T) (decisio.serve.temperature; default: the value fitted on the suite's served readouts); a registered task's own correction replaces it; 1 switches it off (the output before it, bit for bit); never changes the most probable option |
| `--temperature-choice` | - | `float` | /v1/systemone: the temperature for choice questions in place of --temperature (default: the base's; Qwen 1.37, fitted on the suite's choice items; Gemma the global one); 1 switches it off for that type |
| `--temperature-noul` | - | `float` | /v1/systemone: the temperature for noul questions in place of --temperature (default: the global one); 1 switches it off for that type |
| `--temperature-score` | - | `float` | /v1/systemone: the temperature for score questions in place of --temperature (default: the global one); 1 switches it off for that type |
| `--think-temperature-choice` | - | `float` | /v1/systemone: the temperature for the choice answers that thought (the mix of the plain read and the read after the reasoning, --think) in place of the choice temperature (default: a tuned repository's think_temperatures, else the single-pass temperature); whether a question thinks is still decided at the single-pass temperature |
| `--think-temperature-noul` | - | `float` | /v1/systemone: the temperature for the noul answers that thought (the mix of the plain read and the read after the reasoning, --think) in place of the noul temperature (default: a tuned repository's think_temperatures, else the single-pass temperature); whether a question thinks is still decided at the single-pass temperature |
| `--think-temperature-score` | - | `float` | /v1/systemone: the temperature for the score answers that thought (the mix of the plain read and the read after the reasoning, --think) in place of the score temperature (default: a tuned repository's think_temperatures, else the single-pass temperature); whether a question thinks is still decided at the single-pass temperature |
| `--temperatures-file` | - | `FILE` | the base's temperatures from a decisio.adapter/1 file (`python -m decisio.serve.adapter_temperatures fit`, from labelled off-suite reads taken under the layout you serve): per question type and, for choice, by number of options. Precedence: a --temperature-<type> flag, this file, a tuned repository's defaults, the base's profile. The values are in the serving-stack fingerprint, so a certificate made under others is suspended |
| `--noul-commit` / `--no-noul-commit` | - | on or off | /v1/systemone: an output transform on yes/no answers: P(yes) strictly between 0.20 and 0.80 is reported as 0.80 above 0.5 and 0.20 at or below it; the answer never changes, its calibration does. Off by default; a tuned repository's defaults state their own setting, and --noul-commit / --no-noul-commit override it |
| `--over-limit` | - | `refuse`, `truncate` | /v1/systemone: a state over the engine's prompt ceiling. refuse (the default): a 422 that says so. truncate: the state, never a question, is cut once per request to its start, the response says what was cut (header x-decisio-state-truncated, body state_truncated) and none of the request's answers is certified; a request's "over_limit" field decides for that request, and a tuned repository's defaults state their own setting |
| `--batch-invariant` | - | `on`, `off` | vLLM's batch-invariant kernels (VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1, set before the engine starts): every row is computed the same whatever else is in its batch, so a repeated request gives the same answer under load and after a restart. on or off; without it a tuned repository's defaults.batch_invariant decides, else off. A variable in the environment that says the opposite is refused. Costs about 1.03 times a single read on FP8 and 1.6 times on bf16 (12B, one card); the answers are not those of the other kernels |
| `--emulate-precision-casts` | - | `on`, `off`, `auto` | torch inductor's emulate_precision_casts (TORCHINDUCTOR_EMULATE_PRECISION_CASTS=1, set before the engine starts): the compiled kernels keep each bf16 rounding step, which narrows the difference between two cold starts of the same model. auto (the default): on for an FP8 base (the 12B FP8, the 31B served FP8, a tuned repository of either), off for bf16. A variable in the environment that says the opposite is refused. Changes FP8 numerics once compared with releases before 0.33.0 (docs/running.md, "Precision casts") |
| `--header-limit` | `auto` | `auto|off|TOKENS` | /v1/systemone, the header layout: a request whose rows would be over the context because the header lists every question's instructions is answered with a header that lists only the questions that fit, in the request's order (none: the plain layout's row); the response says so (body header_limited, header x-decisio-layout) and a certified task's answer is not certified. auto (the default): the limit is the context; a number: also at most that many tokens of header; off: a row over the context is a 422 that says where its tokens are. A request that fits is not touched |
| `--think` / `--no-think` | - | on or off | /v1/systemone: think when unsure. A question whose served top probability is below its type's threshold (choice 0.75, yes/no 0.92, score 0.70, times --think-factor) and that has at most 16 options is read again after the served model (the adapter named in the request, or the merged weights) has written up to --think-budget tokens of reasoning; the two reads are mixed in log space and go through the type's think temperature if it has one (--think-temperature-<type>), else the same temperature. Off by default (single-pass speed and determinism); a request's "think" field decides for that request, a tuned repository's defaults can turn it on, and --no-think turns that off. Needs the vLLM engine; questions of a registered task stay at one read |
| `--think-factor` | - | `float` | the factor on the think thresholds (default 1; a tuned repository's defaults state theirs): a lower factor thinks on fewer questions |
| `--think-types` | - | `TYPES` | the question types that may think, comma separated: choice, noul, score (default: all; a tuned repository's defaults state theirs). A type outside the list stays at its single read |
| `--think-budget` | - | `int` | the most tokens of reasoning a thinking question may write (default 512) |
| `--over-limit-tokens` | - | `int` | the prompt ceiling in tokens a truncating server cuts to, where it is not the served context less one (default: a tuned repository's defaults.over_limit_tokens, else that; the MLX build, whose limit is a memory budget, needs it for --over-limit truncate) |
| `--tasks` / `--no-tasks` | on | on or off | /v1/systemone: apply registered per-task calibration and intent heads (POST /v1/tasks; decisio.serve.tasks); --no-tasks ignores them (default on; no task, no change) |
| `--tasks-file` | - | text | a JSON list of tasks to load at start (GET /v1/tasks?full=1) |
| `--tasks-dir` | - | text | a directory where taught tasks are kept, one file each, so that a restart does not lose them: every registration, import, certification and removal (calibration tasks and abstention tasks) is written through, atomically, before it is reported, and a write that fails fails the request; everything in it loads at start. With --tasks-file / --abstention-tasks, a task of the file whose id the directory does not hold is saved to it; one it holds stays as the directory has it. One server owns a directory (docs/tasks.md) |
| `--task-store` | - | `URL` | a store of taught tasks that replicas share (s3://bucket/prefix, gs://, az://; needs the obstore package, pip install 'decisio[task-store]'): a task taught on one replica is published as its exact fitted record and the others apply it within --task-store-poll-seconds, without fitting it again; a write names the version it replaces and fails with 409 if the store holds another (?replace=1 overrides); credentials come from the provider's usual chain or environment. An alternative to --tasks-dir (docs/tasks.md, docs/operating.md) |
| `--task-store-endpoint` | - | `URL` | --task-store: the endpoint of an S3-compatible service other than AWS (MinIO, R2, GCS interoperability) |
| `--task-store-poll-seconds` | `5.0` | `float` | --task-store: how often a replica checks the store for tasks taught elsewhere (default 5.0) |
| `--task-store-readonly` | off | on or off | --task-store: this replica applies tasks from the store and does not teach them: registration, certification, import and removal answer 409 (send them to the designated replica) |
| `--require-tasks` | - | `N` | refuse to start unless at least N tasks (calibration tasks of this server's stack, abstention tasks of its served model) are loaded: a lost or empty store must not become untaught answers silently |
| `--head-engine` | off | on or off | read the intent head's hidden state from a second engine (decisio.serve.hidden_engine.HiddenEngine), a second copy of --model in vLLM's pooling mode, instead of from the text engine: faster head questions (one request, not three) for deployments with heavy intent traffic on a dedicated card, at a second weight copy; not co-resident with --image-model (docs/tasks.md) |
| `--head-gpu-memory-utilization` | `0.47` | `float` | the hidden-state engine's share |
| `--debug-readout` | off | on or off | honour the x-decisio-debug header (the raw readout in the response; for reads and diagnostics, not for latency measurement or production: about 130 ms more per single-question request on a 12B) |
| `--one-engine` | off | on or off | load only the --image-model engine (at --gpu-memory-utilization) and serve text requests on it too: the fallback for a card that cannot hold both engines; changes the text route's class |
| `--gpu-memory-utilization` | - | `float` | the text engine's share of the card (default 0.90; 0.47 beside the image engine of --image-model, which needs the pair to fit on the card) |
| `--max-model-len` | - | `int` | the longest prompt, in tokens. Without it, the vLLM server on a Gemma base serves the largest length that fits this card, up to the base's ceiling (gemma-4-12b 65,536, gemma-4-31b 98,304) and not below 32,768; the Qwen base, --image-model, a second engine, --engine-process separate and the other backends stay at 32,768. Given, it is that length, up to the ceiling (docs/running.md) |
| `--kv-cache-dtype` | - | `auto`, `fp8` | the KV cache's data type: auto (the model's, the default) or fp8, which holds twice the tokens and changes the numerics (a task and its certificate are fitted under one; docs/running.md) |
| `--image-gpu-memory-utilization` | - | `float` | the image engine's share of the card (default 0.49, beside the text engine's 0.47); a pair with a default in it may total at most 0.96, a pair given in full at most 1.0 |
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | text | listen address (default: this machine only; put a reverse proxy in front to expose it) |
| `--port` | `8000` | `int` |  |
